analysis.title: Europe Technology: Hardware: Read-across from Nvidia's 3QFY27 results for European AI indexed names
key_insights: Nvidia reported 3QFY27 revenue of $115.8bn, up 103% y/y and 20% q/q, above GSe and Street expectations. Data Center revenue was $107.6bn, up 21% q/q, also above GSe and Street.

Data Center growth came from Hyperscaler and AI Cloud, Industrial and Enterprise customers. Hyperscaler revenue was underpinned by the Vera Rubin ramp and continued Grace Blackwell GPU strength. Rubin generated c.$20bn of revenue in its first quarter of production shipping, the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history (per NVDA).
Nvidia guided 4QFY27 revenue to $130bn at the midpoint, c.4% above Street estimates of c.$125bn. 4QFY27 is a 14-week quarter.
Nvidia raised its FY28 revenue growth outlook to c.75% y/y from c.70% y/y, off a higher FY27 base.

Nvidia said token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May, and demand accelerated: weekly token volumes on OpenRouter are up 35x y/y and 3.5x over the last 3 months. Agentic workloads are c.80% of tokens.
Hopper GPUs are being re-contracted at c.2x their original contract price under multi-year agreements, and B300 rates have risen more than 60% since introduction (per NVDA).
Nvidia reiterated it is on track to launch Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028.
GS sees the raised FY28 outlook, continued demand and roadmap execution as positive for the AI ecosystem and for European AI semicap names ASML, ASMI, BESI and TPRO, all rated Buy.
GS cites its US team's view that unconstrained demand for CY27 remains above supply, which together with the product cadence gives visibility on leading-edge semiconductor demand in the medium term.
On Logic, Nvidia management said agentic AI is driving CPU demand ahead of supply and expects total CPU revenue to more than double in FY28.

GS ranks ASML best positioned in its coverage because of exposure to both leading-edge Logic and Memory, a stronger competitive moat and longer lead times. ASMI, BESI and TPRO should benefit from rising process complexity (ASMI) and advanced packaging and testing requirements (BESI, TPRO).
Nvidia said Sovereign AI revenue more than tripled y/y in 3Q, which GS views as positive for the AI semis ecosystem.

market_movers.rationale: Buy on the Conviction List. Best positioned in GS coverage given exposure to leading-edge Logic and Memory, a stronger moat and longer lead times. Target based on 32x 2HCY27+1HCY28E P/E.
Should benefit from increasing process complexity as AI adoption grows. Target based on 20x 2HCY27+1HCY28E EV/EBITDA.
Should benefit from advanced packaging requirements. Target based on 27x 2HCY27+1HCY28E EV/EBITDA.
Should benefit from advanced testing requirements. Target based on 42x CY28E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: Buy ratings on ASML, ASMI, BESI and TPRO. Higher AI adoption should drive demand for additional leading-edge Logic and Memory capacity.

earnings_insights: Nvidia 3QFY27 (reported 11/17 after US close): revenue $115.8bn, +103% y/y and +20% q/q, above GSe and Street expectations. Data Center revenue $107.6bn, +21% q/q, above GSe and Street.
Nvidia 4QFY27 guidance: revenue $130bn at the midpoint, c.4% above Street estimates of c.$125bn. 4QFY27 is a 14-week quarter.
Nvidia FY28 revenue growth outlook raised to c.75% y/y from c.70% y/y prior, off a higher FY27 base.
Nvidia management expects total CPU revenue to more than double in FY28. Sovereign AI revenue more than tripled y/y in 3Q.
risk_factors: ASML: EUV delays, capex cyclicality and unfavourable market share shifts.
ASMI: worsening of the semi cycle, stronger-than-expected competition and high customer concentration.
BESI: customer spending cyclicality, delays in hybrid bonding adoption and increasing competition.
TPRO: slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, delays in the planned capacity ramp, and large EURUSD movements that could create revenue and earnings volatility.
